recent_posts.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is now generally available
recent_posts.summary: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is now generally available on Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise platform. Positioned as the fastest and most cost-efficient model in the Gemini 3 series, it targets ultra-low latency and high-volume production workloads. Real-world adopters include JetBrains (IDE AI assistant), Gladly (customer service at ~60% lower cost vs. thinking-tier models, p95 latency ~1.8s), Astrocade (game creation with multimodal safety checks), krea.ai (prompt enhancement), OffDeal (real-time financial research agent), Ramp (high-volume latency-sensitive features), and AlphaSense (data processing). The model is suited for agentic tasks like tool calling, orchestration, and automated pipelines at scale.

recent_posts.title: Agentic AI for Public Sector at Google Cloud Next '26
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud Next '26 showcased how public sector organizations including the FDA, U.S. Department of Transportation, and City of Los Angeles are actively scaling agentic AI across their operations. Over 40 public sector speakers shared blueprints for deploying AI agents to boost workforce productivity and transform service delivery. The event featured dedicated programming for national security and research, hands-on agent-building at the Google Public Sector Hub, and 28 live Mission Talks demonstrations. A follow-up Best of Next webinar for public sector attendees is available for registration.

recent_posts.title: Five guides to building production-ready AI agents on Google Cloud
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud has published a five-part series summarizing architecture patterns and best practices for running AI agents in production, tied to the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform announced at Google Cloud Next '26. The guides cover: (1) design patterns for long-running agents with checkpoint-and-resume and human-in-the-loop approval; (2) a five-layer agent governance stack including cryptographic agent identity, centralized tool governance, and behavioral anomaly detection; (3) multi-agent orchestration patterns in Agent Development Kit (ADK) including hybrid graphs and coordinator-specialist patterns; (4) integration patterns using Agent-to-Agent (A2A) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) for cross-organization agent federation; and (5) pre-built Atomic Agent Blueprints in Agent Garden to accelerate production-ready deployments. The platform supports routing tasks across 200+ models including Gemini, Gemma, and third-party models like Claude.

recent_posts.title: Managed Apache Airflow: Scaling Data & AI Workloads
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud has rebranded Cloud Composer as Managed Service for Apache Airflow and announced four major updates. Apache Airflow 3.1 is now generally available, bringing decoupled architecture, DAG versioning, managed backfills, event-driven scheduling, and Human-in-the-Loop support. A Data Engineering Agent powered by Gemini is embedded in the dashboard for agentic troubleshooting of DAG failures. A new declarative orchestration framework lets users define pipelines in YAML without deep Airflow expertise, integrating with dbt, Spark, and other tools via GitHub Actions. Finally, an MCP Server for Managed Airflow is in public preview, exposing tools for agents and developers to query environment and DAG run data directly from their preferred interfaces.

recent_posts.title: Firestore: Agentic AI, Search, and MongoDB Compatibility
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud announced several Firestore updates at Cloud Next '26. Key additions include native integrations with AI Studio, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex via Firestore Skills and a remote MCP service for agentic app development. A new pipeline query engine (GA) brings hundreds of query capabilities including full-text search (preview) powered by Google search technology with strong consistency, geospatial queries, JOIN via subqueries, and bulk data manipulation operators. MongoDB compatibility is expanded with support for larger 16MiB documents, highly scalable change streams for real-time sync to BigQuery, collection drop commands, and flexible TTL offsets. Natural language querying via Gemini Code Assist is also available in preview. All features are part of the Firestore Enterprise edition.

recent_posts.title: Chrome Enterprise introduces new integrations for healthcare
recent_posts.summary: Google is announcing Chrome Enterprise Premium integrations tailored for healthcare organizations. The offering includes advanced data loss prevention, phishing/malware protection, HIPAA compliance reporting, and new partnerships with Epic (EHR optimization), Imprivata (passwordless authentication), AuthX (identity management), and Citrix (unified workflows). A special promotional offer is available for eligible organizations with 1,000+ users, including a 6-month free trial, $5,000 in services funding upon conversion, and technical onboarding with Google and Epic experts.

recent_posts.title: Cloud CISO Perspectives: At Next ‘26, why we’re multicloud and multi-AI
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud COO Francis deSouza outlines the company's multicloud and multi-AI security strategy following Google Cloud Next '26. Key highlights include AI-powered SOC agents reducing threat mitigation time by 90% and cutting alert triage from 30 minutes to 60 seconds, the integration of Wiz for securing AI development lifecycles across clouds, and the launch of the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform with Agent Gateway, Model Armor, and Agent Identity components. The post argues that a durable AI roadmap requires multiple models and cloud providers, and that Google's vertical integration of hardware, AI, and security gives it a day-one advantage in deploying new models to security products.

recent_posts.title: Google Cloud monthly AI announcements roundup
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud's monthly AI roundup covers major announcements from Google Cloud Next, including the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform with four core pillars (build, scale, govern, optimize), new Gemini Enterprise app features like Agent Designer, long-running agents, Projects, and Agent Gallery. Hardware updates include 8th-generation TPUs (TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference). Other highlights include the Agentic Data Cloud architecture, Wiz acquisition completion, new security capabilities for agentic workloads, Gemini Embedding 2 (first natively multimodal embedding model), Veo 3.1 Lite video generation, Claude 4.6 on Vertex AI, Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) for agentic commerce, and BigQuery's natural language Comments-to-SQL feature.

recent_posts.title: How UKG taps workforce intelligence with the Agentic Data Cloud
recent_posts.summary: UKG built People Fabric, a unified data and intelligence platform powered by Google's AlloyDB for PostgreSQL and the Agentic Data Cloud. Facing 126 application teams, dozens of tech stacks, and over 12,000 database instances from acquisitions, UKG created a canonical data model and a custom CDC pipeline to stream changes into AlloyDB in real time. This foundation enables millisecond read-after-write queries, vector search for natural-language experiences, and AI agents that can reason across HR, payroll, and timekeeping data simultaneously. Over 1,000 organizations are already on the platform, with migration savings funding half of the project's cost.

recent_posts.title: Google Cloud Next 26 top announcements for AI startups
recent_posts.summary: Google Cloud's Next '26 conference brought a wave of announcements targeting AI startups. Key highlights include the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — a full lifecycle platform for building, scaling, governing, and optimizing multi-agent systems. The Agentic Data Cloud introduces Cross-Cloud Lakehouse, managed MCP servers for databases, and near-100% text-to-SQL accuracy tools. New compute options include TPU 8t/8i chips (up to 3x training performance, 80% better inference cost-efficiency), Axion N4A instances, and GKE Agent Sandbox with sub-second scaling. Security gets a boost via Google-Wiz integration with automated threat hunting and AI-APP protection. On the go-to-market side, startups can distribute agents via the Agent Gallery in Gemini Enterprise and tap into a new $750M partner innovation fund. A six-week AI Agents Challenge with $90,000 in prizes is also open globally until June 5, 2026.

top_posts.title: Choosing Antigravity or Gemini CLI
top_posts.summary: Google offers two AI-integrated development tools: Antigravity, a complete IDE with agent management and visual development features, and Gemini CLI, a terminal-based tool for command-line and headless execution. Both have generous free tiers, with Gemini CLI having gained significant popularity with nearly 100k GitHub stars. The choice depends on whether you prefer a full IDE experience or terminal-based workflows.

top_posts.title: Introducing Google Cloud Vertex AI Extensions for .NET
top_posts.summary: Google Cloud announces the Google.Cloud.VertexAI.Extensions library, enabling .NET developers to integrate Gemini models on Vertex AI through Microsoft.Extensions.AI abstractions. The library provides a unified API for multi-provider AI applications, supporting chat, embeddings, and image generation. It complements the existing Google Gen AI .NET SDK by offering flexibility for developers who need to work with multiple AI providers (Google, OpenAI, Azure) while maintaining consistent code patterns. The library is currently in beta and includes code samples for common use cases.

top_posts.title: Cloud SQL for MySQL introduces optimized writes
top_posts.summary: Google Cloud SQL for MySQL Enterprise Plus edition now includes optimized writes, a feature that automatically tunes MySQL configurations based on real-time workload metrics to improve write performance. The feature delivers up to 3x better write throughput compared to Enterprise edition, with five automated optimizations that adjust parameters and data handling without manual intervention. The post includes detailed benchmarking instructions using sysbench to measure performance improvements across different instance configurations, demonstrating the benefits for write-intensive OLTP workloads.

top_posts.title: Introducing the Builders Hub from the Google Developer Program
top_posts.summary: Google has launched Builders Hub, a centralized developer workbench within the Google Developer Program. It provides a unified dashboard for Google Cloud, Firebase, and AI Studio projects, personalized learning recommendations based on your tech stack, integrated Google Cloud credits for hands-on Codelabs, digital badges for skill recognition, and a discovery engine for local developer communities and events. The goal is to reduce friction by consolidating scattered consoles and documentation into a single entry point.

top_posts.title: Project management for SREs
top_posts.summary: Managing projects in SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) requires balancing production support with project work. At Google, SREs allocate 50% of their time to production and enhancements. Effective planning, including reserving resources and early engagement of Technical Program Managers (TPMs), is crucial to handle unforeseen challenges and ensure timely project completion. Google's proactive approach has allowed them to manage complex projects while maintaining reliability and compliance.
